title: Yellow Buckeye: Ancient Yellow Buckeyes You Can Visit
meta_description: A buckeye of the Appalachians and the Ohio Valley. Ohio's champion, 31.7 metres tall, was standing before Spring Grove Cemetery was founded in 1845.
intro: Yellow buckeye is a tree of the Appalachians and the Ohio Valley, and the biggest of ours is a local. Spring Grove Cemetery in Cincinnati was founded in 1845, and its own arboretum says this buckeye was already there, a survivor of the woods on the Mill Creek floodplain. It is Ohio's champion today, 4.52 metres round and 31.7 metres tall, and nobody has published how much older than the cemetery it is. The other two were planted. Wisconsin's champion stands near the office of the MacKenzie Center at Poynette, filed in the state register under Aesculus octandra, an older name now treated as a synonym. And on the University of Colorado campus in Boulder, a buckeye the city thinks went in during the early 1900s, after Hale Science was built in 1894, is called one of the largest of its kind in Colorado, a long way from the Ohio River.
